story_comparison.sent_summary: Sri Lanka has begun its third mutual evaluation by the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG), with the inaugural meeting held in Colombo on 26 October. The exercise examines the country's compliance with and practical implementation of international standards on anti-money laundering, countering terrorist financing and countering proliferation financing (AML/CFT/CPF). Speaking at the opening, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya emphasised that a credible framework requires institutions, laws, supervision, investigation and enforcement to work effectively together—not merely to exist on paper. She also highlighted the damage that corruption and weak public trust can cause to financial stability, and recalled Sri Lanka's previous periods of increased monitoring by the Financial Action Task Force. The Government committed to engage with the assessment team and continue addressing weaknesses. The evaluation has started; this is not an announcement of a final rating or outcome.

story_comparison.headline: CRIB expands credit information ecosystem
story_comparison.generated_summary: The Credit Information Bureau of Sri Lanka (CRIB) has announced a significant expansion of the country’s credit information ecosystem with the onboarding of four licenced microfinance institutions, following the publication of the relevant Government Gazette Notification. story_comparison.approved_summary: Sri Lanka (CRIB) has announced a significant expansion of the country’s credit information ecosystem with the onboarding of four licenced microfinance institutions, following the publication of the relevant Government Gazette Notification. This initiative marks an important step towards strengthening credit information sharing within the microfinance sector, enhancing the availability of reliable credit information, and promoting greater financial inclusion by facilitating improved access to formal credit for underserved individuals and businesses.
story_comparison.sent_summary: The Credit Information Bureau of Sri Lanka (CRIB) has brought four licensed microfinance companies into its national credit-information network following a Gazette notification under the CRIB Act. The institutions are Berendina Micro Investments Company, Lak Jaya Micro Finance, Dumbara Micro Credit and Sejaya Micro Credit. As designated lending institutions, they can contribute borrowers' credit information to CRIB and obtain credit profiles through the established information-sharing framework. CRIB said the change extends formal credit reporting beyond the mainstream banking sector and improves visibility of borrowers who have historically had a limited credit footprint. The onboarding was marked at an event attended by CRIB leadership and Central Bank officials. It is an expansion of the reporting ecosystem, not an announcement of new lending volumes or an automatic improvement in borrowers' creditworthiness.

story_comparison.sent_summary: Sri Lanka received 136,096 international tourists during the first 25 days of October 2026, according to Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority figures reported by The Morning. India accounted for 51,424 visitors, or roughly 38% of the month's arrivals to that point. story_comparison.headline: Cabinet approves US$100 million ADB macro-recovery financing
story_comparison.sent_summary: The Cabinet approved entering into a US$100 million financing agreement with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for the Macro-Recovery Sector Development Programme, after the Department of External Resources completed formal negotiations. The package is split evenly between a US$50 million policy-based loan and a US$50 million investment loan, both from ADB's ordinary capital resources. It forms part of a broader US$620 million framework covering five sub-programmes intended to advance economic reforms alongside Sri Lanka's IMF Extended Fund Facility programme. The Cabinet had previously endorsed this macro-recovery programme on 7 September; the latest development is approval to proceed with the negotiated agreement, not evidence of a new US$620 million commitment or funds already disbursed. It is separate from earlier ADB social-protection financing and from the Mahaweli water project financing reported elsewhere in this brief.

story_comparison.headline: Cabinet clears US$60 million OPEC Fund loan for Mahaweli water security
story_comparison.sent_summary: The Cabinet approved proceeding with a US$60 million loan arrangement from the OPEC Fund for International Development to help finance Phase 2 of the Mahaweli Water Security Investment Programme. According to contemporaneous reports of the Cabinet decision, the proposed facility is made up of US$48 million and US$12 million components. Phase 2 has an estimated overall cost of US$536.5 million and is expected to involve multiple development partners; the Asian Development Bank has separately agreed to provide US$200 million towards this water-security programme. Proposed work includes completion of a section of the main water-transfer tunnel, additional canals and irrigation infrastructure, and improvements intended to support dry-zone agriculture and climate resilience. This OPEC facility is for an infrastructure programme and must not be conflated with the separate ADB macro-recovery package.

story_comparison.headline: Apparel exports rise in September but remain lower over nine months
story_comparison.sent_summary: Sri Lanka's apparel exports returned to growth in September 2026 but remained below the previous year's level over the first nine months, according to data highlighted by the Joint Apparel Association Forum (JAAF). Exports for September reached US$416.99 million, up 3.47% from US$403.01 million in September 2025. The United States market grew 7.17% to US$172.03 million, while shipments to the European Union excluding the UK rose 6.5% to US$132.46 million. By contrast, exports to the UK fell 5.92% and sales to other markets also declined. For January–September, total apparel exports stood at US$3,588.46 million against US$3,798.25 million a year earlier, a contraction of 5.52%. These are apparel-industry figures; they should not be confused with aggregate merchandise-export growth reported separately.

story_comparison.generated_summary: Sri Lanka will not reduce its high indirect taxes immediately, Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Anil Jayantha Fernando has said, arguing that the country must first secure stronger revenue mobilisation before it can “reset” a tax structure he acknowledged is burdensome. story_comparison.approved_summary: Sri Lanka will not reduce its high indirect taxes immediately, Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Anil Jayantha Fernando has said, arguing that the country must first secure stronger revenue mobilisation before it can “reset” a tax structure he acknowledged is burdensome. Fernando said the government remains committed to fiscal consolidation, but signalled that tax relief, including a possible reduction in the 18% Value Added Tax (VAT), could become possible once government revenue reaches a more sustainable share of the economy.
story_comparison.sent_summary: In remarks reported late on 27 October, Deputy Finance Minister Anil Jayantha Fernando said Sri Lanka could reconsider its heavy indirect-tax burden only when government revenue is sufficiently secure to support fiscal consolidation and public investment. He acknowledged concerns about the current 18% Value Added Tax (VAT) rate and other taxes, but did not announce an immediate VAT reduction or new tax rate. Fernando said revenue had reached approximately 16.7% of GDP by the end of 2025, exceeding an earlier benchmark, and described a longer-term ambition to move it towards around 18% of GDP by 2030. He indicated that further revenue space would be needed before the authorities could reset the tax structure, while continuing to prioritise infrastructure and other investment spending. The remarks complement, rather than implement, the 2027 Budget proposals described in the capital-markets section.
